title: Mrs Helen Bennis Pinto @ Helen Pinto vs Sri Donald Bharath Pinto on 30 September, 2020

paragraphs.text:
1


 IN THE HIGH COURT OF KARNATAKA AT BENGALURU

 DATED THIS THE 30TH DAY OF SEPTEMBER 2020

 BEFORE

 THE HON'BLE MR.JUSTICE S. SUNIL DUTT YADAV

 CIVIL PETITION No.306/2018
 c/w
 CIVIL PETITION No.142/2019

Civil Petition No.306/2018
Between:
Mrs.Helen Bennis Pinto @ Helen Pinto,
W/o Donald Bharath Pinto,

R/o Bendore Benedictus House,
Mercara Hill, Mangaluru - 575 002. ... Petitioner

Sri.Donald Bharath Pinto,
S/o late Henry Pinto,
Aged about 46 years,
R/at St.Lawrence Estate,
Mundugodu, Karimane,
Jayapura, Koppa Taluk,
Chikmagaluru District - 577 126. ... Respondent

 This Civil Petition is filed under Section 24 of CPC,
praying to transfer the Matrimonial Case in M.C.No.84/2018
filed by the respondent before the Prl. Judge, Family Court,
Chikmagaluru, under Section 32 of Indian Divorce Act for
 2


the relief of Restitution of Conjugal Rights, to the Family

pending on the file of Prl. Family Judge, Mangaluru filed
under Section 10(i) and (x) of the Divorce Act 1989, in the
interest of justice and equity.

Civil Petition No.142/2019
Between:

And:

1. Mrs.Helen Bennis Pinto,
 W/o Donald Bharath Pinto,
 Aged about 46 years,
 R/at Bendore Benedictus House,
 Mercara Hill, Mangaluru - 575 002.(D.K)

2. Ramya Ganiga,
 D/o Mrs.Jayamma,
 Aged about 25 years,
 R/at St.Lawrence Estate,
 Karimane, Jayapur,
 P.O. Jayapur - 577 123,
 Koppa Taluk,
 Chikkamagaluru District. ... Respondents

(By Sri.M.Vishwajith Rai, Advocate for R1;
Service of notice to R2 is dispensed with
v/o dtd:30.09.2020)
 3


 This Civil Petition is filed under Section 24 of CPC,
praying to transfer the Petition in M.C.No.345/2018 pending
on the file of Principal Judge, Family Court, Mangaluru, DK,
to the Principal Judge, Family Court, Chikkamagaluru to be
tried along with M.C.No.84/2018, in the interest of justice
and equity.

 These Civil Petitions coming on for admission this day,
the Court made the following:

 ORDER

The petitioner in CP No.306/2018 is the wife and

has sought for withdrawal of proceedings in

M.C.No.84/2018 filed by the respondent pending before

the Principal Judge, Family Court, Chikmagaluru

wherein the respondent has sought for relief of

restitution of conjugal rights.

2. The petitioner submits that petition has

been filed before the Principal Judge, Family Court,

Mangaluru filed under Section 10(i) and (x) of the Indian

Divorce Act, 1989, seeking for dissolution of marriage.

3. The facts as made out in the petition is that

the petitioner and the respondent had entered into the
 4


wedlock on 19.05.1997 at St. Lawrence Church,

Mallandur, Chikmagaluru Taluk.

4. It is further submitted that from within the

said wedlock they have two children. It is submitted

that the petitioner has been taking care of the children

and they are pursuing their education at Chikmagaluru.

It is submitted that the petition filed seeking dissolution

of marriage is before the Family Court at Mangaluru

and the petition filed by the respondent in M.C.

No.84/2018 seeking for restitution of conjugal rights is

pending before the Family Court at Chikmagaluru. It is

submitted that if the petitioner were to attend the

proceedings at Chikmagaluru, the petitioner would be

required to travel a distance of about 200 Kms. It is

submitted that there is great inconvenience in travelling

such distance which interferes with a right of fair trial

and hence, submits that proceedings instituted by

respondent - husband be withdrawn and transferred to
 5


the Court where M.C.No.345/2018 is pending

consideration before the Family Court at Mangaluru.

5. Learned counsel for the respondent submits

that he has filed a separate transfer petition in

C.P.No.142/2019, wherein he has sought for transfer of

proceedings in M.C.No.345/2018 pending before the

Principal Judge, Family Court at Mangaluru to be

withdrawn and transfer to the Court at Chikmagaluru

to be tried along with M.C.No.84/2018.

It is submitted that wife had instituted

proceedings seeking relief of partition in

O.S.No.116/2018 which was pending before the Court

of Senior Civil Judge, Chikmagaluru and subsequently

the said plaint has been ordered to be returned with

liberty to represent the same before the Family Court at

Chikmagaluru and accordingly, the wife would not be

prejudiced, if the proceedings instituted by her is

withdrawn and transferred to Chikamagaluru where
 6


the proceedings relating to partition are directed to be

instituted.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner however

submits that insofar as the matrimonial disputes are

concerned there could be consolidation.

8. Insofar as proceedings initiated in

M.C.No.84/2018 by the respondent - husband seeking

for restitution of conjugal rights and M.C.No.345/2018

filed by the wife seeking for dissolution of marriage, it is

clear that in light of the possibility of conflicting

decrees, looking in to the nature of relief sought for,

there has to be consolidation of both the proceedings.

No doubt the fact that the proceedings in partition are

to be resumed by re-presentation of the plaint before the

Family Court at Chikmagaluru is accepted by the

learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner -
 7


wife. However, insofar as the proceedings relating to

restitution of conjugal rights and dissolution of

marriage, the same could be consolidated irrespective of

the possibility of proceedings in partition being

continued before the Court at Chikmagaluru. It is also

to be noted that the proceedings in partition on the one

hand and the petitions for dissolution of the

matrimonial relationship and restitution of conjugal

rights on the other are to be tried Separately.

9. The convenience of the wife is a matter that

could be taken note of despite the assertion of the

counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent -

husband that the petitioner would be required to travel

to Chikmagaluru to prosecute the proceedings in

partition. However, taking note that the dispute relating

to partition could be tried separately while the allegation

and material available as regards the proceedings in

restitution of conjugal rights and dissolution of
 8


marriage to a great extent being common material and

raising common allegations by each party against the

other, the said proceedings would call for consolidation,

it would be appropriate taking note that the distance

between Mangaluru and Chikmagaluru is about 150

Kms to withdraw the proceedings in M.C.No.84/2018

pending before the Principal Judge, Family Court,

Chikmagaluru and transfer to the Family Court at

Mangaluru to be tried along with M.C.No.345/2018.

10. Accordingly, the petition is allowed. The

proceedings in M.C.No.84/2018 pending on the file of

Principal Judge, Family Court, Chikmagaluru is to be

withdrawn and transfer to the Principal Judge, Family

Court at Mangaluru.

11. The records pertaining to M.C.No.84/2018

pending on the file of Principal Judge, Family Court,

Chikmagaluru to be transmitted to the Principal Judge,

Family Court at Mangaluru forthwith.

12. In light of the order passed in CP

No.306/2018, CP No.142/2019 seeking for relief of

transfer does not survive for consideration.

13. Insofar as the CP No.142/2019, though it is

noted that 2nd respondent has not been served, notice is

dispensed with insofar as the 2nd respondent is

concerned in light of the fact that 2nd respondent is

stated to have remained exparte in the proceedings

before the Family Court and also noting that the main

dispute is between the husband and the wife while the

2nd respondent in CP No.142/2019 has been arraigned

in light of the allegations made that she has illicit

relationship with the husband of the present petitioner.
Accordingly, the petitions are disposed off.
